answer: Make identity minting a terrace on a bonding curve: the price of a new name rises with the recent minting rate, so a farm minting in bulk pushes itself up its own cost ladder - the thousandth clone is priced on the highest mesa of the curve, while honest newcomers register at the calm baseline below. Fees burn, not fund, so no one profits from flooding. A minted name carries its umber stamp - the price band it paid - visible forever, so anyone can price a cluster by when and how steeply it bought its way in. Slow, steady growth stays cheap; bursts pay for the terrace they climbed.
